title: Machine learning identifies SLC6A14 as a novel biomarker promoting the proliferation and metastasis of pancreatic cancer via Wnt/beta-catenin signaling.
authors: Dang, Cunshu; Bian, Quan; Wang, Fengbiao; Wang, Han; Liang, Zhipeng
one_liner_zh: 该研究用机器学习筛选胰腺癌诊断标志物并验证SLC6A14经Wnt通路促进肿瘤进展，属纯肿瘤生物标志物与信号通路研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) has the poorest prognosis compared to other common cancers because of its aggressive nature, late detection, and resistance to systemic treatment. In this study, we aimed to identify novel biomarkers for PC patients and further explored their function in PC progression. We analyzed GSE62452 and GSE28735 datasets, identifying 35 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between PC specimens and non-tumors. Based on 35 DEGs, we performed machine learning and identified eight diagnostic genes involved in PC progression. Then, we further screened three critical genes (CTSE, LAMC2 and SLC6A14) using three GEO datasets. A new diagnostic model was developed based on them and showed a strong predictive ability in screen PC specimens from non-tumor specimens in GEO, TCGA datasets and our cohorts. Then, clinical assays based on TCGA datasets indicated that the expression of LAMC2 and SLC6A14 was associated with advanced clinical stage and poor prognosis. The expressions of LAMC2 and SLC6A14, as well as the abundances of a variety of immune cells, exhibited a significant positive association with one another. Functionally, we confirmed that SLC6A14 was highly expressed in PC and its knockdown suppressed the proliferation, migration, invasion and EMT signal via regulating Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway. Overall, our findings developed a novel diagnostic model for PC patients. SLC6A14 may promote PC progression via modulating Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. This work offered a novel and encouraging new perspective that holds potential for further illuminating the clinicopathological relevance of PC as well as its molecular etiology.
abstract_zh: 胰腺癌（PC）与其他常见癌症相比，预后最差，原因在于其侵袭性强、发现晚以及对全身治疗耐药。在本研究中，我们旨在为PC患者识别新的生物标志物，并进一步探讨其在PC进展中的功能。我们分析了GSE62452和GSE28735数据集，在PC标本与非肿瘤组织之间鉴定出35个差异表达基因（DEGs）。基于这35个DEGs，我们进行了机器学习，并识别出8个参与PC进展的诊断基因。随后，我们利用三个GEO数据集进一步筛选出三个关键基因（CTSE、LAMC2和SLC6A14）。基于这些基因，我们开发了一个新的诊断模型，该模型在GEO、TCGA数据集及我们自己的队列中，从非肿瘤标本中筛选PC标本时表现出强大的预测能力。接着，基于TCGA数据集的临床分析表明，LAMC2和SLC6A14的表达与晚期临床分期及不良预后相关。LAMC2和SLC6A14的表达以及多种免疫细胞的丰度之间表现出显著的正相关。在功能上，我们确认SLC6A14在PC中高表达，其敲低通过调控Wnt/β-catenin信号通路抑制了增殖、迁移、侵袭及上皮-间质转化（EMT）信号。总体而言，我们的研究为PC患者开发了一个新的诊断模型。SLC6A14可能通过调节Wnt/β-catenin信号促进PC进展。这项工作提供了一个新颖且有前景的视角，有望进一步阐明PC的临床病理相关性及其分子病因学。
